goal.statement: Let returning users sign in from a one-time link sent to their email, so nobody needs a password to reach their account.

doneWhen.text: Entering a registered email sends a sign-in link
Opening the link signs the user in once and returns them to the page they came from
A used or expired link shows a clear error with a way to request a new one
Unknown emails get the same response as known ones
Requests are rate-limited per email and per IP

keyChanges.title: One-time tokens, stored hashed
keyChanges.text: A new magic_link_tokens table keeps a SHA-256 hash, an expiry and a used-at time, so a leaked table cannot be replayed.

keyChanges.title: Two new auth routes
keyChanges.text: POST /auth/magic-link issues and emails a token; GET /auth/verify consumes it and creates the existing session cookie.

keyChanges.title: A second path on the login form
keyChanges.text: An "Email me a link" action sits beside the password flow and leads to a check-your-inbox state.

decisions.question: How long should a link stay valid?
decisions.reason: 15 minutes. It covers slow email delivery while keeping a forwarded link short-lived.

decisions.question: Where should rate limits be enforced?
decisions.reason: Redis. It is already used for sessions and holds across instances.

decisions.question: What if the link opens on a different device?
decisions.reason: Sign in on that device. Most people read email on their phone, and a short lifetime limits the exposure.

edgeCases.text: The same link is clicked twice
The link is opened one second after expiry
The email is typed with different casing
Two links are requested and the older one is opened
A mail scanner fetches the link before the user does

manualChecks.text: Send a real link to Gmail and Outlook and sign in from each
Request on a laptop, open the link on a phone
Sign in with a password to confirm nothing regressed

risks.title: Email security scanners open links automatically and use up the token
risks.fallback: Make the verify page show a "Continue" button, and only consume the token on that click.

risks.title: Slow email delivery means links expire before they arrive
risks.fallback: Raise MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MINUTES without a deploy, and keep the resend action one click away.

risks.title: The per-IP limit blocks people who share an office network
risks.fallback: Treat the per-email limit as primary and loosen the IP threshold.

assumptions.text: Email addresses are unique and already verified
Redis is available in every environment
The existing session cookie logic can be reused as is

openQuestions.text: Should requesting a new link cancel the earlier ones?
Do magic-link sign-ins need their own audit log entry?
Who signs off the wording of the email?
